Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-28 14:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Julia Hammond (AsterTech Head of Security), Marcela Ruiz (AsterTech Legal), Ben Cho (AsterTech Platform)

Auto-generated Summary (brief, may be incomplete):
Redwood walked through their data residency controls, region-affinity routing, KMS options including BYOK and escrow, subprocessor notification practices, and audit artifacts (SOC 2 / ISO). Customer asked for stronger contractual guarantees around EU-only processing for certain PII, clarified subprocessors list and change-management, and asked about audit logs, RBAC, SSO/SCIM provisioning. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO docs, subprocessor inventory, draft contract clause, and schedule technical POC for EU-pinning.

Topics: Data residency and region pinning, cross-border processing, KMS/BYOK options, subprocessors & supply-chain, SOC2/ISO artifacts, RBAC/SSO, audit log retention

Action items (auto): see action_items field above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Speaker 1 (Samira): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Diego, our solutions engineer. How's the audio?
[00:06] Speaker 2 (Diego): can you hear me okay? mic's a bit low.
[00:09] Speaker 3 (Julia): yes, loud and clear. thanks.
[00:11] Speaker 1 (Samira): Great. quick agenda — high-level security posture, region pinning mechanics, KMS/BYOK options, subprocessors lifecycle, and then Q&A. we'll try to leave 15 minutes at end for legal specifics.
[00:24] Speaker 4 (Marcela): that works. from legal side we'll want any contractual text for the EU-only processing guarantee. not just an implementation note.
[00:30] Speaker 2 (Diego): totally understood. I can walk through how our routing policy works and what we can enforce at the control plane versus what needs to be expressed in the contract.
[00:37] Speaker 5 (Ben): quick context from platform — we run in aws eu-west and us-east; we need assurance that model inference and logs with EU-personal data never leave EU without explicit authorization. also curious about KMS separation.
[00:48] Speaker 1 (Samira): got it. Julia, could you outline the scope of "EU-only" for you — is it strictly inference compute plus logs, or also backups, metrics, and metadata?
[00:57] Speaker 3 (Julia): primarily inference and logs that include PII; backups we can discuss but prefer keep backups in region too. metrics are ok to be aggregated outside EU if pseudonymized.
[01:07] Speaker 2 (Diego): OK. so our platform supports region affinity and region pinning at route and workspace level. practically that means requests from your EU routes can be routed to EU-hosted inference nodes only. For the things that can leak, we have three control layers — routing policy, data plane enforcement, and contractual subprocessor restrictions.
[01:23] Speaker 4 (Marcela): can you confirm whether telemetry and audit logs contain raw prompt text? that's a risk for us.
[01:30] Speaker 2 (Diego): by default, logs capture request IDs, latency metrics, model versions, and token counts. We do have optional request body logging for debugging but it's disabled for EU pinned tenants unless you opt in. there may be edgecases in third-party monitoring agents — we can disable those.
[01:43] Speaker 3 (Julia): that's good but we need proof — SOC 2 artifact that shows log sampling and redaction policies.
[01:49] Speaker 1 (Samira): yes we can share SOC 2 Type II report and our ISO 27001 certificate. we'll put the redaction and logging controls in the security pack.
[01:56] Speaker 5 (Ben): about KMS — we want customer-managed keys for EU data and ideally HSM-backed. does Redwood support BYOK or customer KMS integration?
[02:04] Speaker 2 (Diego): we support two main KMS models: Redwood-managed keys (standard) and BYOK via customer-managed KMS (we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). For BYOK you upload a key or configure a key policy and we reference it from the EU region. For HSM-only escrow, we have an enterprise option that plugs into dedicated HSM endpoints — that's usually part of Private deployments.
[02:21] Speaker 4 (Marcela): when you say "reference it from the EU region" — can you guarantee the key material never leaves the EU?
[02:27] Speaker 2 (Diego): yes — if you configure an EU KMS key and restrict key policy to EU principals and endpoints, the key material lives in the EU region. our service calls KMS endpoints in-region for envelope encryption. the unencrypted data never leaves the region when the route is pinned.
[02:41] Speaker 3 (Julia): what's your fallback behavior if EU capacity is saturated? we can't have cross-border failover without legal approval.
[02:48] Speaker 2 (Diego): good question. our default is to fail closed (reject requests) if region pinned capacity is exhausted, but we can configure a controlled fallback with explicit allow-listing to specific regions — this is only available with Dedicated or Private deployments and must be contractually approved.
[03:04] Speaker 5 (Ben): Is there a way to have policy-level audit that shows every time fallback was considered? we need an immutable trace.
[03:11] Speaker 2 (Diego): yes, audit logs capture routing decision events, including reason codes (capacity, health, policy). those are included in the customer-facing audit stream and can be forwarded to your SIEM in EU via webhook or syslog.
[03:23] Speaker 4 (Marcela): subprocessors — please send the current list and your policy for notifications and objections. we need at least 30 days notice before adding a processor that could access EU data.
[03:34] Speaker 1 (Samira): our standard subprocessor notification window is 30 days; customers can object within that period and we either remove or proceed with approved contractual mitigations. we'll attach our subprocessor inventory and the DPA language that covers notification and right to object.
[03:45] Speaker 3 (Julia): do you use any third-party observability agents that might ship data to the US? we had an incident with another vendor where traces were forwarded.
[03:53] Speaker 2 (Diego): we use a combination of first-party telemetry and vetted third-party services. For EU-pinned tenants, we can disable third-party forwarders and route observability to an EU-only endpoint; we also support forwarding to your own collector. we'll include the list in the pack.
[04:08] Speaker 5 (Ben): how about supply-chain — small question: who builds/compiles the runtime and where is it stored?
[04:15] Speaker 2 (Diego): the runtime is built in our CI in EU and US build farms; artifacts are signed. for customers requiring EU-only supply chain, we can arrange dedicated build pipelines as part of private/on-prem packages. signing keys are rotated and stored in KMS.
[04:30] Speaker 3 (Julia): would you provide SBOMs and build attestations?
[04:33] Speaker 2 (Diego): yes — we provide SBOMs and can provide signed build attestations on request.
[04:38] Speaker 4 (Marcela): any third-party subprocessors in the US that could see EU data?
[04:42] Speaker 1 (Samira): standard list includes CDN provider, metrics aggregator, and a managed storage provider; for EU-pinned customers, we route to EU instances of the same providers where possible. we'll send the full inventory.
[04:53] Speaker 3 (Julia): on RBAC and SSO — how do you manage admin access across environments?
[04:58] Speaker 2 (Diego): we integrate with SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC supports workspace roles (admin, engineer, auditor) and token scoping. for enterprise, we support time-bound elevation and session MFA enforcement.
[05:11] Speaker 5 (Ben): do you support session recording or long-lived API keys for automation? we prefer short lived tokens.
[05:17] Speaker 2 (Diego): short-lived tokens via our OAuth flow and support for rotating service principals is the default. long-lived keys are discouraged and can be restricted.
[05:24] Speaker 3 (Julia): how long do audit logs retain? we need 12 months of immutable audit for compliance.
[05:29] Speaker 2 (Diego): default retention is 90 days; we have configurable retention tiers up to 7 years as an add-on. immutable retention snapshots and export to your archive are supported under enterprise contracts.
[05:40] Speaker 1 (Samira): marking a note — add retention options to the security pack.
[05:44] Speaker 4 (Marcela): can you include the exact fields you keep in audit trails? we need user id, action, timestamp, request URL, decision reason, and routing decision.
[05:53] Speaker 2 (Diego): yes that's all captured — we'll extract schema and send.
[05:57] Speaker 3 (Julia): about data deletion — if we delete a user or dataset, is that propagated to backups and K/V caches? we need proof of logical delete and a timeline for physical deletion.
[06:06] Speaker 2 (Diego): deletes trigger asynchronous workflows; logical delete is immediate, physical purge from live stores occurs within a configurable window (default 30 days), and backups follow a separate retention purge schedule unless you opt-in for immediate purge which we offer under private agreements. we'll document timelines.
[06:22] Speaker 3 (Julia): what's the process for emergency legal requests from other jurisdictions — how do you notify customers?
[06:29] Speaker 1 (Samira): we have a legal process for government requests and a transparency report. we push notifications to the customer's security contact and log the request in the audit stream. for EU-pinned customers we also apply an additional review before any export.
[06:41] Speaker 4 (Marcela): competitor question — how do you compare to MegaModelCloud's regional guarantees?
[06:45] Speaker 2 (Diego): MegaModelCloud offers region affinity but often has implicit fallback; our differentiator is fail-closed defaults for region pins, and contractual guardrails to force Dedicated/Private for sanctioned cross-border fallbacks.
[06:59] Speaker 5 (Ben): ok. Marcela — any legal blocking points for us today?
[07:03] Speaker 4 (Marcela): we'll need to review the exact DPA language and the subprocessor addendum. Also the BYOK clause and key escrow terms — if there's an escrow mechanism it needs to be auditable.
[07:14] Speaker 1 (Samira): absolutely. we'll provide a draft with specific language.
[07:18] Speaker 3 (Julia): on the technical POC — what would Diego need from us to stand up an EU-pinned test?
[07:24] Speaker 2 (Diego): ideally a small test workspace, sample inputs (pseudonymized), and a KMS key (or we'll demo with Redwood-managed EU key). we'll also need the specific routes you want pinned and any RBAC constraints.
[07:36] Speaker 5 (Ben): timing wise we can provision a workspace early next week.
[07:40] Speaker 1 (Samira): great. we'll note that as a next step.
[07:44] Speaker 2 (Diego): quick note on encryption-in-transit — our control plane uses mTLS between control and data planes; data plane communications are TLS1.3 with forward secrecy.
[07:53] Speaker 3 (Julia): do you support hardware-backed attestation for the data plane nodes?
[07:57] Speaker 2 (Diego): we support optional AMD SEV and Intel TDX for dedicated/private nodes and can provide attestation artifacts. for hosted, we use cloud VM attestations — we can include evidence.
[08:10] Speaker 4 (Marcela): can we require that any subprocessor in the US who processes EU-pseudonymized data cannot export raw text off-region?
[08:18] Speaker 1 (Samira): contractual restriction possible. operationally, we route such processing to EU instances of those subprocessors; where not possible we use alternatives or remove the subprocessor for that customer.
[08:29] Speaker 3 (Julia): what's your SLA if we choose Dedicated? important for us is latency and guaranteed region availability.
[08:36] Speaker 2 (Diego): Dedicated comes with committed capacity and region SLAs; we can commit to multizone EU deployments and reserved GPU pools. we'll provide the SLA doc.
[08:46] Speaker 5 (Ben): backlog question — how are model updates handled for pinned workloads? do you get automatic model pushes?
[08:52] Speaker 2 (Diego): customers can pin model versions; we support canary rollouts and manual approval. auto-updates are off by default for pinned workspaces.
[09:00] Speaker 3 (Julia): great, that covers model drift concerns.
[09:03] Speaker 1 (Samira): quick pause — any other high-level things?
[09:06] Speaker 4 (Marcela): we've flagged one redline in procurement: a clause preventing any third-party transfer of EU personal data unless consented. can you provide a DPA language that maps to that?
[09:15] Speaker 1 (Samira): yes. we'll propose language that aligns with standard EU DPA with right to object to subprocessors and a 30 day notice window.
[09:23] Speaker 2 (Diego): technical note — for routing we attach geo-coordinates and region tags at ingress; those tags are used by the scheduler to place work on region-compliant nodes. that tag is immutable for a request once ingress validation passes.
[09:37] Speaker 3 (Julia): important. and the tag is recorded in audit logs?
[09:40] Speaker 2 (Diego): yes, request tag and decision published in audit event.
[09:44] Speaker 5 (Ben): do you support custom retention timelines per dataset?
[09:48] Speaker 2 (Diego): yes — dataset-level retention controls are available in Private/Dedicated; hosted customers can request custom retention tiers as part of enterprise plan.
[09:57] Speaker 4 (Marcela): can you promise data residency in the contract only for on-prem or also for hosted?
[10:03] Speaker 1 (Samira): we offer contractual residency guarantees for hosted with region pinning, but for the strongest assurance we typically recommend Dedicated or Private packages — hosted gets standard guarantees plus technical controls; Dedicated/Private can get explicit escrow, no-fallback clauses, and stronger attestations.
[10:20] Speaker 3 (Julia): do you have any customers with similar constraints you can reference? even anonymized would help.
[10:25] Speaker 1 (Samira): yes — a European fintech client uses Dedicated with BYOK and has a no-fallback clause; we can provide a sanitized case study.
[10:34] Speaker 2 (Diego): moving toward Q&A from technical side — any requests for the POC specifics?
[10:39] Speaker 5 (Ben): we'd like an EU-only POC hitting a small model endpoint, plus the routing audit stream forwarded into our SIEM. also test a simulated capacity saturation to see fail-closed behavior.
[10:50] Speaker 2 (Diego): noted. we'll prepare a test plan for the POC.
[10:54] Speaker 3 (Julia): on-subprocessor consequence — if you add a subprocessor in the US, what's the approval flow?
[10:59] Speaker 1 (Samira): we notify customers 30 days in advance. if you object, we either remove the subprocessor for you or proceed with supplemental safeguards.
[11:09] Speaker 4 (Marcela): is there any recording of requests that happen in the control plane that might carry personal data?
[11:14] Speaker 2 (Diego): control plane logs include user IDs and resource ids but not full request payloads. data plane handles payloads; we have separation of duties to minimize exposure.
[11:24] Speaker 3 (Julia): can we get a diagram of separation?
[11:28] Speaker 2 (Diego): yes, we'll include architecture diagrams highlighting separation boundaries.
[11:31] Speaker 1 (Samira): wrapping up — agreed next steps and action items as in the notes. I'll summarize and follow up in email with attachments.
[11:40] Speaker 5 (Ben): one last thing — do you offer an indemnity for data breaches caused by subprocessors?
[11:46] Speaker 1 (Samira): typical indemnity language is limited; we do have breach notifications and incident response commitments, plus cyber insurance. we'll share the legal team contact and typical indemnity language as a draft.
[11:58] Speaker 3 (Julia): alright thanks, we look forward to the security pack.
[12:01] Speaker 1 (Samira): thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.
